scope: Ranks 251–1500, resolved current similar-word teaching and typed recall. Includes retained baseline cards; do not infer no synonyms from unchanged status.
grading: Only exact headword/explicit alternatives pass after case/edge-punctuation normalization. Accent/spelling slips and recognized inflections get score-free correction opportunities, not immediate rejection. Dictionary-form recall is explicit. Cloze and recognition acceptance are separate. Broad main teaching examples may show a different legitimate sense from selected typed cue; classify teaching alignment separately from false facts.

sections.title: To finish
sections.text: Terminar, acabar and concluir overlap for finishing an activity. Acabar de + infinitive also describes something just done; that construction is different.

sections.title: To answer
sections.text: Responder and contestar overlap when answering a question. Responder de means answer for or take responsibility for something.

sections.title: To cause
sections.text: Causar, provocar and ocasionar can describe causing a problem. Provocar also means provoke a person; that additional meaning is not automatic for the other verbs.

sections.title: To cross
sections.text: Cruzar and atravesar overlap for going across a street. Cruzar also describes crossing one's legs; atravesar can describe piercing or going through something.

sections.title: To remain
sections.text: Permanecer means remain. Quedarse commonly expresses staying behind or staying in a place; plain quedar has other uses, such as something remaining available.

sections.title: To place
sections.text: Colocar, poner, situar and ubicar overlap for placing something. Their broader uses differ: poner has many change-of-state constructions, and situar/ubicar emphasize location.
examples: Coloca la mesa junto a la ventana.
Place the table next to the window.

sections.title: To remove
sections.text: Quitar and retirar overlap for removing something. Sacar specifically suggests taking it out of somewhere; not every removal has that direction.
examples: Retira el vaso de la mesa.
Remove the glass from the table.

sections.title: To stop
sections.text: Detener and parar overlap when stopping a vehicle. Detener also means detain someone; detenerse is the usual reflexive form when the subject stops.

sections.title: To throw
sections.text: Echar, lanzar and tirar can describe throwing a ball. Tirar also means throw away, and tirar de means pull on; echar has many fixed expressions.

sections.title: To include
sections.text: Incluir, incorporar, agregar, añadir and sumar all fit adding a name to a list. Integrar emphasizes bringing parts into a whole; integration can involve more than listing something as included.
examples: Incluye su nombre en la lista.
Include his name on the list.

sections.title: To express
sections.text: Expresar and manifestar overlap for expressing an opinion. Manifestar can also make a condition evident; manifestarse can mean demonstrate in public.

sections.title: To guarantee
sections.text: Garantizar and asegurar overlap in giving assurance. Asegurar also means secure physically or insure; those uses require their own context.

sections.title: To state
sections.text: Afirmar emphasizes asserting truth. Declarar can be a statement, especially a formal one; a declaration need not be a claim of certainty.
examples: She states that it is true.

sections.title: To assert
sections.text: Afirmar asserts something as true. Declarar can also state it, often formally; it does not always imply certainty.

sections.title: To declare
sections.text: Declarar can make a statement; afirmar asserts. Declarar also has special uses such as declaring income or declaring love.

sections.title: To keep
sections.text: Conservar and mantener overlap for keeping something in a condition. Guardar emphasizes keeping or storing it; storage does not necessarily mean preservation.
examples: Conserva los documentos en buen estado.
Keep the documents in good condition.

sections.title: To care for
sections.text: Cuidar and atender overlap in looking after someone. Atender can also mean attend to a request; asistir a means attend an event.

sections.title: To buy
sections.text: Comprar means buy. Adquirir can mean acquire by purchase but also by other means, so acquire alone does not entail payment.

sections.title: To break
sections.text: Romper and quebrar overlap for breaking a solid object. Quebrar also describes bankruptcy; romper has a wider range of everyday collocations.

sections.title: To protect
sections.text: Proteger and defender overlap for protection. Defender emphasizes defending against a threat and also applies to arguing for a position.

sections.title: To gather
sections.text: Reunir and juntar overlap for bringing things together. Reunirse and juntarse describe people getting together.

sections.title: To agree
sections.text: Acordar means agree or decide together. Acordarse de means remember and overlaps with recordar; removing se changes the verb's use.

sections.title: To solve
sections.text: Resolver and solucionar overlap for solving a problem. Resolver can also mean decide or settle a matter.

sections.title: Beginning
sections.text: Principio, inicio and comienzo overlap for a beginning. Principio also means a principle; that ethical or theoretical sense is separate.
examples: El inicio del curso es mañana.

sections.title: Reason
sections.text: Motivo and razón overlap for a reason to act. Causa names what produces an effect, which need not be someone's conscious motive.
examples: Explica el motivo de su decisión.
She explains the reason for her decision.

sections.title: Concept
sections.text: Concepto is a concept or notion. Idea is broader and can be a proposal or thought, so not every idea is a defined concept.

sections.title: Route
sections.text: Camino, ruta and vía overlap as ways of reaching a destination. Camino can be a physical path; vía can also be a means or railway track.

sections.title: School
sections.text: Escuela and colegio overlap for schools, with differences in local education systems. Colegio can also be a professional association; universidad is a different educational level.

sections.title: Teacher
sections.text: Profesor and maestro overlap for a teacher. Maestro also means master or expert, and the preferred term for a schoolteacher varies by place and level.

sections.title: Student
sections.text: Estudiante and alumno overlap for a school student. Alumno emphasizes the relationship to a teacher or institution; estudiante emphasizes studying.

sections.title: Job
sections.text: Trabajo, empleo and puesto overlap for a job. Trabajo also means work generally, while puesto emphasizes a particular position.
examples: She is looking for a job.

sections.title: Task
sections.text: Tarea names a task; labor and trabajo can describe the work involved. Trabajo also names employment, while una tarea can be unpaid or schoolwork.

sections.title: Question
sections.text: Pregunta directly names a question asked. Cuestión may be a question under discussion, and asunto/tema mean a matter or topic rather than necessarily a question sentence.

sections.title: Matter
sections.text: Asunto, cuestión and tema overlap for a matter under discussion. Tema also means a theme or topic, and cuestión can be a question or problem.

sections.title: Face
sections.text: Cara and rostro overlap for a face. Rostro can sound more formal or literary; cara also means a side or surface.

sections.title: Floor
sections.text: Piso and suelo overlap for a floor surface. Piso also names a storey or an apartment in some regions; those meanings are separate.
examples: El suelo de la cocina está limpio.

sections.title: Room
sections.text: Habitación and cuarto overlap for a room. Sala commonly names a larger or public room or a living room; not every room is a sala.

sections.title: Home
sections.text: Casa and hogar overlap for home. Vivienda emphasizes a dwelling or housing; hogar also evokes home life and can mean hearth.

sections.title: Husband
sections.text: Marido and esposo both mean husband. Novio means boyfriend or groom and does not by itself mean husband.

sections.title: Mom
sections.text: Mamá is a familiar form of madre. Madre is the neutral relationship term; mamá has final stress and an accent.

sections.title: Boy
sections.text: Chico and muchacho overlap for a boy or young person. Niño specifically suggests a child; the applicable age range depends on context.

sections.title: Food
sections.text: Comida and alimento overlap for food. Comida also means a meal, whereas alimento can be one foodstuff or nourishment.

sections.title: Event
sections.text: Evento, suceso and acontecimiento overlap for an event. Evento often names an organized occasion; suceso can refer to an incident.

sections.title: Increase
sections.text: Aumento and incremento overlap for an increase. Crecimiento is growth, which may be physical, numerical or developmental.
examples: There was an increase in prices.

sections.title: Mistake
sections.text: Error and equivocación overlap for a mistake. Error also has technical meanings in measurement or computation.

sections.title: Stage
sections.text: Etapa and fase overlap for stages of a process. Etapa also names a leg of a journey or race.

sections.title: Newspaper
sections.text: Periódico and diario overlap for a newspaper. Diario can also mean diary, and as an adjective means daily.

sections.title: Daily
sections.text: Diario and cotidiano overlap for daily. Periódico means recurring at intervals, not necessarily every day.

sections.title: Language
sections.text: Lengua and idioma overlap for a named language. Lenguaje can describe the human faculty, a system of expression or a style of language; it need not identify a national language.

sections.title: Exhibition
sections.text: Exposición and muestra overlap for an exhibition. Muestra also means a sample, while exposición has senses of explanation and exposure.

sections.title: Feature
sections.text: Característica and rasgo overlap for a distinguishing trait. Rasgo also describes a stroke or facial feature.

sections.title: Near
sections.text: Próximo and cercano overlap for spatial nearness. Próximo also means next; cercano does not replace it in every future-time expression.

sections.title: Real
sections.text: Real and verdadero overlap for genuine or real. Verdadero also means true rather than false; real can also mean royal.

sections.title: True
sections.text: Cierto and verdadero overlap for true. Before a noun, cierto can mean a certain or some, which does not assert truth.

sections.title: Fundamental
sections.text: Básico and fundamental overlap for foundational importance. Básico can also mean elementary rather than advanced.

sections.title: Large
sections.text: Grande is general size. Enorme emphasizes very large, while amplio emphasizes breadth or spaciousness; they are not always equivalent degrees or dimensions.

sections.title: Serious
sections.text: Grave and serio overlap for a serious problem. Serio can also describe a person's sober manner, while grave can describe a low-pitched sound.

sections.title: Expert
sections.text: Experto is an expert. Especialista specializes in a field, and profesional practices an occupation; the labels overlap but do not guarantee the same expertise.

sections.title: Behind
sections.text: Detrás de explicitly relates a position to something else. Atrás often means backward or at the back and can also describe past time; usage with complements varies regionally.

sections.title: In front
sections.text: Delante de gives a position in front of something. Adelante commonly gives a forward direction or encouragement to proceed.
examples: It is in front of the house.

sections.title: Approximately
sections.text: Cerca de and alrededor de can express approximation. Without that numerical construction, cerca means nearby and alrededor means around.
examples: There are about a hundred people.

sections.title: To take on
sections.text: Here asumir means taking on a duty or responsibility. It can also mean taking something as true, overlapping with suponer; that is a separate sense, not an incorrect use.

sections.title: To save
sections.text: Salvar is saving or rescuing from danger. Guardar is keeping or storing something, such as saving a file.

sections.title: To save
sections.text: Guardar is the usual verb for saving a file. Salvar commonly means rescue; file-saving terminology can vary by software and region.

sections.title: To appear
sections.text: Aparecer and surgir overlap when something comes into view or emerges. Aparecer also means turn up, including after being missing.

sections.title: To arise
sections.text: Surgir emphasizes emergence or arising. Aparecer can also describe something appearing, without specifying how it developed.

sections.title: To laugh
sections.text: Reír means laugh; sonreír means smile. A smile does not necessarily involve laughter.

sections.title: To smile
sections.text: Sonreír means smile, while reír means laugh. They describe related but distinct actions.

sections.title: To warn
sections.text: Advertir and avisar can warn of danger. Advertir also means notice, but notar does not replace it for warning someone.

sections.title: Spanish
sections.text: Español and castellano both name the Spanish language. Castellano can also refer specifically to Castile in other uses.

sections.title: Congress
sections.text: Congreso can be a conference or a legislative body. Conferencia can also be a lecture or conference; the legislative meaning is separate.

sections.title: Conference
sections.text: Conferencia and congreso overlap for conferences. Conferencia also means lecture, while congreso may name a legislature.

sections.title: Advantage
sections.text: Ventaja is an advantage; beneficio can be a benefit. Beneficio also means profit, which is not always a comparative advantage.

sections.title: Benefit
sections.text: Beneficio and ventaja overlap for a benefit or advantage. Financial profit is another sense of beneficio.

sections.title: Genre
sections.text: Género names a genre or a kind and also gender. Sexo concerns sex; the terms are not interchangeable across all uses.

sections.title: Eyesight
sections.text: Vista and visión overlap for eyesight. Vista also names a view; visión can name a vision or perspective.

sections.title: Vision
sections.text: Visión and vista overlap for visual ability. A vision of the future is another use of visión.

sections.title: News item
sections.text: Noticia is news or a news item. Mensaje is a message, which need not report news.

sections.title: To aim
sections.text: Apuntar can mean aim or note down. Indicar and señalar can point something out, but do not substitute in every weapon-aiming construction.

sections.title: Scene
sections.text: Escena is a scene; escenario can be a stage or setting. A performance's scene and its physical stage are distinct.

sections.title: Stage
sections.text: Escenario is a stage or setting. Escena can name a dramatic scene rather than the physical platform.

sections.title: Painting
sections.text: Cuadro can mean painting, chart or a group. Tabla overlaps with a chart, not a painted picture.

sections.title: Piece
sections.text: Pieza can be a piece or, regionally, a room. Cuarto matches the room sense, not every component.

sections.title: Destination
sections.text: Destino can mean destination or fate. Sino overlaps with fate, not a travel destination.

sections.title: Alive
sections.text: Vivo can mean alive, vivid or lively. Intenso overlaps with vivid intensity, not being biologically alive.

sections.title: Equal
sections.text: Igual expresses equality. Mismo can express identity; equal quantities need not be the very same object.

sections.title: Equally
sections.text: Adverbial igual can mean equally, or perhaps in informal speech. Quizá overlaps only with the possibility sense.

sections.title: Working day
sections.text: Jornada commonly names a working day or day's activity. Día is the general word for day and also fits this selected use.

sections.title: Final
sections.text: Final and último overlap for the last item in a sequence. Final also means conclusive; último is also used for latest.
